name: Function-Level Resource Lifecycle State Machine
description: Formal state machine specification for tracking system resource handle lifecycles along function CFG paths

states.description: Resource handle successfully acquired via supported API contract
Resource handle explicitly released via registered release method along execution path
Resource release registered via top-level function defer statement, guaranteeing execution on all normal and panic exits
Resource ownership transferred to caller via return value or consuming contract
Resource handle stored in long-lived state or passed across unverified boundary
Reachable normal exit paths terminate without explicit or deferred release, with zero clean exits
Resource is released along some exit paths but leaks on error or conditional paths, or release is deferred inside a loop
Resource ownership cannot be statically determined (e.g. opaque struct encapsulation or reflection)

supported_resources.special_semantics: defer Rollback() followed by Commit() is safe in Go; Rollback after Commit is a documented no-op.

safety_invariants: Every tracked acquisition must terminate in a defensible lifecycle outcome on all reachable function exit paths.
Acquisition error check branches (if err != nil { return err }) immediately following acquisition represent failed acquisition; unacquired exits are pruned from leak accounting.
Deferred releases inside loop bodies are flagged as RESOURCE_LEAK_PROBABLE due to descriptor accumulation across iterations.
Unresolved lifecycles (RESOURCE_UNRESOLVED) are marked INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and never eligible for autonomous remediation without human confirmation.
